title: This Supergirl Movie Set Is a Secret Thank-You to a Comic Book Artist!
summary:
Imagine walking onto a movie set so big it fills an entire building. The ground is covered in rubble. Giant, broken buildings tower over you. Neon signs flicker from what used to be shops. That's what it felt like to visit the set of the new "Supergirl" movie in England. But here's the coolest part: the name of this ruined city is a secret Easter egg for comic book fans.

The city is called Evely, and it's on a planet named Bilquis. If you've read the amazing comic "Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow," those names might ring a bell. The comic was drawn by an artist named Bilquis Evely! The movie is based on her and writer Tom King's story. By naming the set after her, the filmmakers are giving a giant high-five to the artist who helped create this version of Supergirl.

The crew on set kept saying this is director Craig Gillespie's movie, not just another superhero flick. They used real, hand-painted backdrops instead of digital screens to make everything feel more real. The city of Evely is a dying world, and it's where Supergirl (played by Milly Alcock) and her friend Ruthye will face the villain Krem and his space pirates. So when you watch the movie, remember that the amazing ruined city is also a tribute to the artist who dreamed up this Supergirl's look.
why_it_matters: When you watch a movie, look for tiny hidden clues—filmmakers often hide secret messages just for fans who pay close attention, like a fun puzzle.

background_read: Supergirl first appeared in comics in 1959 and is known as Superman's cousin from the planet Krypton.
Bilquis Evely is the artist who drew the 2021 comic series 'Supergirl: Woman of Tomorrow,' which gave Supergirl a fresh new look and story. Tom King wrote the words for that same comic.
Movie makers often hide tiny details—called Easter eggs—in scenes as a secret wink to fans who know the original comics well.
Article_Structure: WHO: The filmmakers of the new 'Supergirl' movie, led by director Craig Gillespie.
WHAT: They named the ruined city 'Evely' on planet 'Bilquis' as a secret tribute to comic artist Bilquis Evely.
WHERE: On a huge indoor set in England filled with rubble, broken buildings, and flickering neon signs.
WHY: To honor the artist who created this version of Supergirl's world and to give comic book fans a hidden surprise.

perspectives.description: Fans feel seen and respected when filmmakers honor the original artists. Finding an Easter egg like Evely's name makes them smile and feel connected to the creators.
Some might say this detail is so small that most viewers will never notice it. But the best Easter eggs are exactly like that—a secret 'hello' to the people who care the most.

Hiding tributes inside a movie is a tradition that shows respect. Director Craig Gillespie seems to want audiences to know this is not just another superhero flick—it's a story built on one artist's vision.
